notes: Chunk E: topic M4.S28.T28 'Questions: Icosahedron and Dodecahedron' (6 pairs, concepts C124-C135).

The book's picture of the two solids (page 12) is used by four question items (C124, C126, C128, C130): one identical diagram per item, with the two names added under the solids (the book prints none).
The solution of C129 (faces at a vertex) marks one vertex per solid; the solution of C135 draws the LP sample answer, a cube frame of straws and clay balls (not printed in the book).
The three straw-and-clay models printed on the page are only illustration for the open-ended last question and are not drawn.
See map/notes_E.md for judgement calls, LP text issues and the borderline list.

figure_inventory.description: Dodecahedron (left solid): A dodecahedron drawn in 3D from the front, faces shaded in alternating tones of violet/purple and pale pink, black outline edges with hidden edges shown as thin dashed lines. Visible faces are regular pentagons: one big pentagon facing the viewer (pale pink) with 5 further pentagons around it (top: dark violet, upper-left: dark violet, right: violet, lower-left: light violet-pink, lower-right: dark violet), 6 pentagons visible; the silhouette is a ten-sided outline. No labels (the two names are blanks in the question).

Icosahedron (right solid): An icosahedron drawn in 3D from the front, faces (equilateral triangles) shaded in alternating violet and pale pink, black outline edges, hidden edges shown as thin dashed lines. A central down-pointing triangle faces the viewer (pale pink) with a ring of triangles around it, a top vertex at the centre top where 5 triangles meet and a bottom vertex at the centre bottom; the silhouette is a hexagon-like outline. No labels.

Icosahedron of P12-solid-2 drawn again in the solution figure of M4.S28.T28.C129, with one vertex ringed and its 5 faces shaded and numbered.

A skeleton model made of blue clay balls joined by pale-tan straws: 6 balls and 12 straws (counted): one ball at the top, one at the bottom and four balls around the middle (left, right, one at the back that is smaller, one at the front); each of the top and bottom balls is joined by a straw to each of the 4 middle balls (8 straws) and the four middle balls are joined in a ring of 4 straws. This is an octahedron skeleton (8 triangular faces).

A skeleton model made of green clay balls joined by pale-yellow straws: 6 balls and 9 straws (counted). One ball at the apex at the top, two balls at the middle left and right (joined to each other by a horizontal straw and each joined to the apex), one larger ball at the centre front (joined to the apex by a thick straw), two balls at the bottom left and right (joined to each other by a horizontal straw, and each also joined to the centre-front ball); each middle-side ball is joined by a straw down to the bottom ball on the same side. So two triangles (the top one: apex + the two middle balls; the front one: centre-front ball + two bottom balls) joined by 3 straws: a triangular prism skeleton.

A skeleton model made of pink clay balls joined by pale-turquoise straws: 10 balls and 15 straws (counted), a two-pentagon frame joined by 5 straws: i.e. a pentagonal prism skeleton drawn in perspective (balls: one at the top, upper-left, upper-centre, small upper-right, a front-middle one, a right-middle one, a small lower-left one, a lower-right-middle one, and two at the bottom left and bottom right).
